105163.recordsNote: No pre-closure custody agreement found. Electronic transcripts for 2001+ graduates via Parchment; hard-copy files claimed by the Chapter 7 trustee (ITT Educational Services estate, S.D. Ind.); some states later recovered records through litigation/settlement (MHEC 2018, Texas 2018 settlement).
105163.notes: Chain-wide shutdown of ITT Educational Services on 2016-09-06, announced the same day, effective immediately; Chapter 7 filed 2016-09-16. ED had barred new Title IV enrollments on 2016-08-25, and ITT said on 2016-08-30 it would let current students finish, so students had effectively no notice. teachOut coded n/a under SHEEO's 'abrupt, no plan possible'; Mass. BHE says no teach-out or transfer options were offered (ED offered closed-school discharge or credit transfer, and some states arranged transfer pathways afterward). IPEDS close dates of 2017-09-03 (Boise, Fort Wayne, St Petersburg; Nashville is in the Tennessee group) and 2016-09-06 (Oak Brook, Orland Park, Springfield IL) are reporting-cycle artifacts: ITT ceased all operations in Sept 2016 (Fort Wayne confirmed individually by Indiana CHE). Boise and St Petersburg were not individually confirmed, they are assumed within the chain-wide closure. 'closed' date is the instruction-cessation date; ED's formal Title IV eligibility loss followed the bankruptcy (2016-09-16). Merger coded none: no acquirer or buyer identified in sources read.

evidence.claim: Official ED page: on September 6, 2016 ITT Technical Institutes announced closing its 130+ campuses; Chapter 7 petition filed September 16, 2016 (S.D. Ind.); all ITT Technical Institutes lost Title IV eligibility.
ED email to students dated Sept 6, 2016: students affected by the announcement of closure of the institution on September 6, 2016; options were closed school loan discharge or credit transfer.

Massachusetts BHE: ITT 'suddenly announced the closure of all of its campuses' on Sept 6, 2016; all instruction ceased as of Sept 6; 'no teach-out period or transfer options were offered to students'; student-record location/availability still argued in Chapter 7.
Indiana CHE fact sheet: ITT announced closure Sept 6, 2016 and closed all 136 locations including Fort Wayne and South Bend.

Aug 25, 2016 ED bar on new Title IV enrollments; Aug 30 ITT said current students could finish; Sept 6 announced closing all campuses 'effective immediately'; Sept 16 Chapter 7. No campus sale or acquirer described.

Note a BPPE emergency order of March 2019 still lists 'Art Institute of California - Inland Empire (Satellite)' as an approved Argosy location, which may just be licensing records; the broader DCEH collapse (receivership, Title IV cut off 27 Feb 2019, all remaining campuses ceased instruction 8 Mar 2019) may have affected students here. I did not find a campus-specific teach-out, abruptness, or records custodian (transcripts for DCEH schools were routed via Parchment and the Arizona State Board for Private Postsecondary Education per Maryland MHEC, but that is system-wide, not confirmed for California). 448628.notes: Parent: Alta Colleges Inc. (ACICS-accredited). Enrollment suspended chain-wide 2015-11-11/12 (not itself a closure announcement). Dec 2015 Durbin letter reports Westwood said it would teach out/end operations at many campuses incl. its four Illinois campuses. Closure announced to students by email ~2016-01-25 (Wikipedia, citing the school email); press reported it 2016-01-27 (CBS Colorado, Inside Higher Ed 'announced Wednesday'); so announced date coded to month. January 2016 term was the last term; campuses closed by 2016-03-08 (ABC7, Wikipedia citing Westwood's 2016-03-29 acknowledgment of closure of all campuses effective 2016-03-08). Abrupt=false is a judgment: roughly six weeks of notice plus partner-school transfer path (credits accepted at same or lower tuition; transfer deadline 2016-02-19), but no formal teach-out found, Westwood acknowledged credits generally would not transfer, and ABC7 reports students were told they could finish at Westwood before being told to transfer (students 'scrambling'); a reviewer could reasonably code this abrupt or teachOut 'no'. Records custodian not established from pages I could read (IBHE pages, which a search summary said point to Parchment for transcripts, were unreachable; not verified). Per-campus differences not checked beyond Illinois/Colorado coverage. Wikipedia's campus list also names Houston campuses not in this batch.

evidence.claim: Enrollment suspended 2015-11-12; email to students 2016-01-25 that college would close in March after January term; all 15 campuses closed effective 2016-03-08 per Westwood's 2016-03-29 acknowledgment; transfer options to partner schools but no formal teach-out described; owner Alta Colleges Inc.
Closure reported 2016-01-27: campuses close in March at end of semester; students told to choose a partner school by mid-February.

Emails told students they must transfer by 2016-02-19; January 2016 term last term; campuses close by March 8; partner schools agreed to accept credits at same or lower tuition; enrollment stopped 2015-11-11; students said they had been told they could finish at Westwood.
Westwood announced (Wednesday, 2016-01-27) it will shut down in March; stopped enrolling in November; no teach-out/transfer detail.
2015-12-14: Alta suspended enrollment 2015-11-12; Westwood will teach out and end operations at many campuses incl. four Illinois campuses and may seek to sell others (attempted sale not confirmed).

'closed' date is the instruction-cessation date; ED's formal Title IV eligibility loss followed the bankruptcy (2016-09-16). Merger coded none: no acquirer or buyer identified in sources read.

474702.notes: IPEDS flags these units 'combined' into a state-level University of Phoenix unit (or Arizona for Online/Phoenix/Southern Arizona), mostly in 2014; Eastern Washington was combined into the Online Campus in 2010. University of Phoenix is a single HLC-accredited institution that reports many campuses (FY2014 10-K), so this is read as a reporting restructure, not an institutional closure; no non-IPEDS source describing the 2014 restructure was found, hence low confidence. SHEEO closure fields left null because they apply only to closures. Caveats: individual campuses in this list may have physically closed on their own timeline, either under the Oct 2012 plan to close 115 locations (a WTOC item names 'the Columbus campus' and the Atlanta learning center as closing, probably Columbus GA = unit 443881) or later in 2017-2024; this group does not describe those physical closures. Search budget ran out before per-campus checks were possible.

evidence.claim: FY2014 10-K: University of Phoenix is regionally accredited by HLC as one institution operating ~110 ground campus locations; the plan to close 115 locations began FY2013 (context for single-institution structure; does not itself describe the IPEDS reporting change).

487393.recordsNote: No records-retention agreement or external custodian found. The college's own site directs transcript requests to a Florida Career College transcript portal and phone line; custodian after closure unconfirmed.
487393.notes: Whole chain (owner International Education Corporation, IEC) closed together: Dept of Education terminated Title IV eligibility in April 2023 (ability-to-benefit testing misconduct), college stopped enrolling new students, stayed open so existing students could finish, IEC announced 2024-01-25 that FCC would shut permanently effective 2024-02-15. 'closed' is the formal shutdown date from news coverage, not the Title IV loss date (April 2023, with aid possibly continuing to Sept 2023 under conditions); SHEEO's definition would point to 2023, so a human should decide which to use. IPEDS exit year 2025 is a reporting lag. Sources name no individual campuses (about a dozen FL/TX campuses); all seven members are assumed to be covered by the chain-wide closure, with no member-specific evidence (Houston/TX campus in particular not confirmed separately). Teach-out is described as teaching out remaining students at FCC itself (finish programs); the Education Dept also worked with state officials and the accreditor to help students find other schools; no written teach-out plan document was seen. Announcement-to-closure window was 3 weeks but students had been on notice of federal-aid loss since April 2023, hence abrupt=false.

evidence.claim: announced: IEC announced January 25, 2024 that FCC would shut permanently effective February 15, 2024; Education Dept terminated FCC aid certification April 2023; FCC withdrew COE accreditation January 2024; Dept worked with state officials and accreditor to help students enroll elsewhere.

announced/closed/teachOut: dated Jan 26, 2024; spokesman confirmed closure; college will formally close by Feb 15 after teaching out all remaining students; had stopped enrolling new students since April 2023.

context: April 2023 Dept of Education cut off FCC aid; about a dozen campuses across Florida and Texas; students could keep aid through September if conditions (e.g. transfer agreements) were met, otherwise ended April; owned by International Education Corp since 2014.
closure: college announced it would close by February 15, 2024 and stayed open so students could finish programs (cites Inside Higher Ed Jan 26, 2024).
closure/records: homepage states Florida Career College has closed permanently and directs transcript and records requests to a phone line and transcript portal (no external custodian named).
